name: slew-r20
airframe: Fighter1, Multirole1, SmallFighter1, trainer, VTOLTrainer1, EW1, FastBomber1, Darkreach
note: ARM B - THE LIMITER EFFECTIVELY REMOVED. OutputSlew pinned at 20.0. NOTE THE CORRECTION TO THE PROPOSED DESIGN: the Cfg bind is AcceptableValueRange<float>(1, 20), so 30 is NOT reachable - 20 is the ceiling and the lever is 3.33x, not 5x. At 20 stick/s the onset frequency for the field amplitude A = 0.5 moves from 1.91 Hz to 6.4 Hz, i.e. above anything this loop produces, so arm B should be limiter-free in the band of interest. OutputSlew IS THE LAW ONLY NONLINEARITY AND HAS NEVER BEEN VARIED ONCE. It is a rate limiter in series with all three axes (_outP/_outY/_outR through MoveTowards(..., OutputSlew*dt)), it reads slew=6.0 in ALL 3,327 captures across ALL 35 batches, and it appears in no standing doc. A rate limiter is the textbook Category-II PIO generator: unity gain and zero phase lag while unsaturated, up to -90 deg of added lag once the commanded sinusoid peak rate exceeds the limit. Onset frequency for A*sin(2*pi*f*t) is f_onset = R / (2*pi*A). WHY THAT IS THE FIRST MECHANISTIC CANDIDATE FOR THE FIELD WOBBLE. Ledger O11 field report: outR swinging +/-0.5 stick, so f_onset = 6/(2*pi*0.5) = 1.91 Hz - and the field complaint is a ~2 Hz roll limit cycle. R43 tried to reproduce it and got outR peak-to-peak 0.004-0.025, i.e. A ~ 0.012, f_onset ~ 80 Hz: R43 was STRUCTURALLY INCAPABLE of exciting the limiter, which is a better explanation of its clean 12-of-12 than 'the servo cannot self-sustain'. The limiter does bind on shipped cards - 284 fully-railed intervals of 241,729, and Darkreach place-deflect spends 10.3 pct of intervals above 2 stick/s with a max of 6.06, the rail itself. THE STIMULUS, AND WHY IT IS NOT place-deflect VERBATIM. place-deflect excites the limiter but is unusable as a wobble card: one Darkreach lane, 2 s legs, and all 24 of its scored segments are RAILED on aoaLimiterActivePct 100 pct at its 95 m/s entry - no signal. This card keeps the excitation and drops the rail: a continuous 40 s azimuth REVERSAL TRAIN, +/-6 deg flipping every 1.0 s, so every edge is a 12 deg step - exactly oblique-12 step size, which the corpus certifies unrailed (oblique-12-c blendRailPct 2.7 pct mean, 2 railed segments of 296) - but 40 edges in 40 s instead of 4 in 32 s. Edge COUNT is what buys limiter engagement; edge SIZE is what buys rails, so the design maximises the first and holds the second at a proven-safe value. Flown at 250 m/s on the eight keys that clear the envelope gate there, which also removes the low-q AoA rail that killed place-deflect. TAG IS fine* ON PURPOSE. scorecard.compute_segment routes fine_track to wobble_scan (stickFlipRate*, wobbleEpisodes*, wobbleFreqHz*, wobbleCoherence*) plus pointing plus overshoot, and saturation_metrics runs for every non-arm type so all four RAIL_METRICS are still published. It gives up the allocation block (rollYawOpposedPct, bothActivePct, rollBlendMean), which this card does not need - the question is one axis and one nonlinearity. READ THE ROWS, NOT ONLY THE SEGMENTS. Index --with-rows: the primary evidence is the occupancy of |d(outR)/dt| at the pinned limit, which no segment metric reports. wobbleFreqHz* will also see the 0.25 Hz forcing of the reversal train itself; the PIO, if present, is a SEPARATE peak an order higher, so read wobbleCoherenceOutR and the raw rate occupancy rather than trusting a single dominant-frequency estimate. SCORE THE PAIR, NEVER ONE CARD. Distinct tags because compare-runs.py keys segments by tag alone. CARD-OWNED VALUES (v1.0.3): throttle 0.70, fuel 1.00, forceEntry true, deck 0, stagger 3 - the values e3-marker-ff and oblique-6-c actually flew in R41/R44. repeat 5 = 4k+1 per X27. count 16 = the clamp, 8 keys x 2 lanes, roster divides evenly, 64 scored segments per arm. PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTION FOR THE PAIR: if the roll oscillation is rate limiting, then (a) the railed-interval count and the fraction of intervals above 2 stick/s FALL sharply from the 6.0 arm to the 20.0 arm; (b) stickFlipRateR falls with them; (c) any oscillation frequency that resolves scales with R, i.e. f(20) / f(6) ~ 3.3 for a fixed amplitude; and (d) terminalOffDeg / rmsPointingErrorDeg do NOT get worse - a limiter that is only there to stop jerk should cost nothing in accuracy when relaxed. FALSIFIED IF: the frequency is independent of R (then it is not the limiter and O11 needs another mechanism), or if raising R makes stickFlipRateR / wobbleCoherenceOutR WORSE - which would be the more interesting outcome, because it would mean the limiter is currently SUPPRESSING a faster instability and is load-bearing rather than incidental. Also falsified, differently, if BOTH arms show zero limiter engagement: then the stimulus is too weak and the amplitude has to go up before the pair means anything - check that first, it is one query over the rows. RECORDER PINNED TO 60 Hz (CAPTURES-DB gotcha 21): at the default 20 Hz the recorder decimates a ~60 Hz loop with no anti-alias filter and the autocorrelation lag is an integer, so reportable frequencies land on a comb of 1/(k*0.0625) -- 2.29/2.67/3.20 Hz with empty bins between, +/-12% at the 1.9 Hz onset this card predicts. This card's RESULT is a frequency, so it cannot fly at 20 Hz. Pinned per-card, not globally: FlushRows=50 counts ROWS, so a global raise would triple main-thread flushes and re-create the freeze AutoFlush=false exists to prevent.
